newsitem.title: INDIA: Jardine lowers East India Hotels to hold.
newsitem.headline: Jardine lowers East India Hotels to hold.

text.p: Jardine Fleming India Broking said on Friday it lowered East India Hotels to a "hold" though it continued to be bullish on the firm's earnings growth over the next couple of years.
Analyst Priya Uppal said the majority of East India's expansion projects would be through group companies. The hospitality firm also planned to expand its international operations.
The company received approval for a $100 million issue of global depositary receipts at its annual shareholders meeting on Wednesday to fund some of these projects.

"No details have been furnished on these projects or the timing of the issue. We are downgrading our recommendation from a buy to a hold in spite of attractive valuations, as we do not see the stock outperforming the index in the light of these uncertainties," Uppal said in a note to investors.
She continued to be bullish on East India's earnings capacity over the next two years.
"We expect a net profit of 1.5 billion rupees for 1996/97 (April-March) and 1.86 billion for 1997/98," she said.
The firm recorded a net profit of 1.2 billion rupees in 1995/96, up from 580.7 million a year ago.
East India's share had outperformed the index by 35 percent in the last one year, Uppal added.
